scope: Within the accepted two-aircraft F02 risk fleet, extend the base aircraft LRU removal subtask to 15 hours while keeping the fit subtask one third hour, for a 15-and-one-third-hour SURP. Test an actually performing repair subtask at hour 60 and describe any inbound spare assignment only from native evidence.

accepted_sibling.relationship: Sibling branch changes route duration to test transit/waiting; this branch changes base removal duration to test labor-performing repair. Neither result implies the other.

source.boundary: No claim about internal inventory reservation follows from a stock issue or mission preassignment. The completed F02.var04 transit slice established an open SURP waiting for an item (terminal NSYWI=1/NSYRP=0), not active repair work. The new two-field duration change aims to isolate that complementary terminal state.

pre_run_hypotheses: The complete authored delta is SystemRepair.SURPT 0.5→15-and-one-third hours and matching TaskBreakDown E01-SURP seq1 <REMOVE> DURN one-sixth→15 hours. Fit DURN stays one-third; all other cells, seed, mission schedule, stock, resources and 60-hour collection remain exact. Verify all populated tables after import/export.

Guarded session-0 SSH import/export/calc/JSON report should complete with global mutex and GUI PID 13340 preserved. Require zero converter errors, only reviewed warning #108, Notes 0 and valid nonempty results. Any converter duration mismatch, semantic warning or invalid SXO excludes this version.

Observe fault, aborted risk mission, base SURP creation, stocked depot LRU demand/transport, and the aircraft removal subtask directly. The removal subtask should start before hour 60 and remain active at the cutoff with P-MAINT booked. Check actual native timing; do not assume a 15-hour duration is interpreted literally or that the parent's random event prefix is identical.

Reconcile any depot LRU arrival and base backorder clearing separately from whether the spare is issued or held for the unfinished aircraft task. Do not call the spare a reservation without an explicit native reservation event or state and a sound definition of that term. The failed installed LRU should not appear at the depot before the long removal completes.

Reconcile all 120 System, Stock and Resource half-hour bins with event-derived repair, stock and worker intervals, the terminal aircraft/resource balances, mission outcomes, and PM wait/completion. Distinguish system actively under repair (NSYRP) from waiting for an item (NSYWI) and from a PM task object created but not performing.

Accept only the active-repair terminal state directly evidenced by native output, sealed raw files, exact source/diff, author replay and separate independent read-only replay. Preserve a rejected candidate as a versioned excluded diagnostic.
limits: One seed, two aircraft, one base/depot route, one artificially long LRU removal and one 60-hour cutoff. No generic reservation or repair scheduling rule is inferred.
Post-cutoff completion, other repair durations, larger fleets, GUI visual behavior and cross-engine equivalence remain unverified.
